title: Cap. IX: Responsio 2 — ὡς ἔπος εἰπεῖν softens bold Levi speech; not Adam-imputation foundation
pass_a_gloss: As Garissoles reports the second reply: the Apostle foresaw that his coming remark on Levi's tithing in Abraham would look hard. He therefore occupied the ground in advance by saying that in Abraham Levi himself also was tithed, with the tag ὡς ἔπος εἰπεῖν ('so to speak'). A softening of that sort appears only when the phrasing is too bold or too uncommon to be pressed hard or used as a step in a proof. Placeus concludes: do not turn this into a gathering that Adam's sin is imputed to all people, and do not bed it as a foundation under a claim that is obscure by itself or that strips itself of credit.
pass_b_english: The second reply, then, as he reports it, is this: the Apostle, foreseeing that what he was about to say about Levi's being tithed in Abraham would seem harsh, forestalled the point by saying, "In Abraham even Levi himself was tithed" — ὡς ἔπος εἰπεῖν, "so to speak." Softening of that kind is used only where the speech is bolder, or more unusual, than one may press hard, or draw a conclusion from by reasoning. This, then, must not be twisted so that from it one gathers that Adam's sin is imputed to all, or so that it is laid under as a foundation for a matter which, of itself, is either obscure, or altogether takes away its own credit.
source_text: Responsio igitur secunda, eo referente, est, Apostolum, quia praevidebat fore, ut durum videretur, quod dicturus erat de decimatione Levi in Abrahamo, praeoccupasse dicendo, In Abrahamo decimatus est & ipse Levi, ὡς ἔπος εἰπεῖν, ut ita loquar. Quae ratio molliendi non usurpatur, nisi ubi locutio audacior est, aut inusitatior, quam ut eam liceat urgere vehementius, aut ex ea quippiam colligere ratiocinando. Hoc igitur non debet eo traduci, ut inde colligatur peccatum Adami omnibus imputari, aut ut tanquam fundamentum substernatur rei, quae ipsa per se vel obscura est, vel omnino fidem ipsa sibi derogat.
